name: Fast Path/Gap
purpose: A visual aid to illustrate the different roads an initiative can take.
why: We will highlight the consequences when standardized assessments (decision-making) are not followed.
whereUsed: The Fast Path/Gap is best used in the Problem Space during the Awareness Phase (1.0) to highlight the results stakeholders get based on the decision- making approach they take. It’s also useful in the Solution Space to remind stakeholders the probable consequences of skipping (past, present, future) decision-making phases and activities.
outcomes: Recognition that variation wastes time, people, resources, and capital
Agreement that the use of standards eliminates variation
Willingness to consider the use of a standardized assessment (decision-making) process

spaces.heading: IF WE ARE IN THE “PROBLEM SPACE” WE NEED TO:
steps: Compare and contrast the two roads an assessment or an initiative can take.
Document ways to stay on the “Fast Path” and avoid falling into “The Gap”.
Emphasize the importance of “checking-in” routinely to avoid falling into “The Gap”.
Reinforce if/when “The Gap” occurs there must be a concerted effort to get back on the “Fast Path”.

spaces.heading: IF WE ARE IN THE “SOLUTION SPACE” WE NEED TO:
steps: Remind stakeholders the importance of using standardized assessments (decision-making).
Acknowledge it is common to go back and forth between the Fast Path and The Gap.
Assess the status of an assessment or initiative (On the Fast Path, Falling into The Gap, In The Gap).
Identify a course of action and assign owners to stay/get on the “Fast Path”.
